hints: 42° and 48° add up to 90°. What do complementary angles share, and which of the two climbs higher?
worded:
1. Range depends on sin 2θ: sin 84° = sin 96°, so R₁ = R₂. (42° and 48° are 45° ∓ 3°.)

2. Height depends on sin²θ, which grows with θ for angles up to 90°. So the 48° projectile rises higher: H₁ \< H₂.

3. So R₁ = R₂ and H₁ \< H₂. (B)

4. Check: the steeper throw also stays up longer, which is why it can rise higher and still land at the same place.
mistakes: Equal ranges do not mean equal heights: the steeper of the pair always goes higher.
Ranges are equal for θ and 90° − θ only on level ground.
